title: The Fermi Paradox: Where Is Everybody?
executive_summary: The Fermi Paradox is the apparent contradiction between high estimates of the probability of the existence of extraterrestrial civilizations and the lack of evidence for, or contact with, such civilizations.
image_caption: The Allen Telescope Array used in SETI radio searches for extraterrestrial intelligence.

key_sections.title: The Drake Equation
key_sections.content: Formulated by Frank Drake in 1961, the Drake Equation estimates the number of active, communicative extraterrestrial civilizations in the Milky Way galaxy based on star formation rates, exoplanet frequency, and technological lifespans.

key_sections.title: The Great Filter Hypothesis
key_sections.content: The Great Filter theory suggests there is a formidable evolutionary barrier preventing intelligent life from surviving to become space-faring—either behind us (e.g. origin of life is rare) or ahead of us (e.g. self-destruction).

key_sections.title: Zoo Hypothesis and Quiet Skies
key_sections.content: Other solutions propose that advanced civilizations avoid contact to let Earth develop naturally (Zoo Hypothesis), or communicate using signals beyond our current detection capabilities.
